title: A formally unramified morphism has a universal first order thickening, unique up to unique isomorphism
statement: Let $h:Z\to X$ be a formally unramified morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-formally-unramified-morphism]. Then there exists a universal first order thickening $Z\subset Z'$ of $Z$ over $X$ [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening]. It is unique up to unique isomorphism: if $(Z'_1,i_1:Z\to Z'_1,h'_1:Z'_1\to X)$ and $(Z'_2,i_2,h'_2)$ are two universal first order thickenings of $Z$ over $X$, there is exactly one morphism $\varphi:Z'_1\to Z'_2$ with $h'_2\circ\varphi=h'_1$ and $\varphi\circ i_1=i_2$, and $\varphi$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 04F3 (lemma-universal-thickening), with the uniqueness remark of Section 04F2 (section-universal-thickening), opening paragraph
